title: Hard reset on G6 breaks transmitter
body: Had no luck getting xdrip to work with my G6 - it said there was an unusual sensor failure and asked if I wanted to hard reset. When I did, it lost contact with the transmitter entirely, and now I can't even get the Dexcom App to find it, so looks like it's trashed.

comments.body: That doesn't sound good. Could you take a screenshot of the `System Status` page (G5/G6 tab) which contains all the details about transmitter battery etc and email it to me jamorham at gmail dot com (to avoid exposing any personal information) Thanks.

Apologies, jamorham - it would have been smart of me to save that information, but I didn't want to wait to get a new transmitter/sensor up and running, and I've already uninstalled xdrip as a precaution to avoid any further interference. I'm know that others have had success with xdrip and G6, so it's not a criticism of the app per se, but I wanted to warn that hard resetting might pose problems in some cases.

Understood. The condition where you would get that message implies the transmitter has already failed. Do you know the rough age of it or battery status? Can you also confirm that your new transmitter firmware version ends in either 23 or 25? Thanks.
it works with firmware 1.6.5.25. It was reconnected after 7 minutes instead 10-15min at G5. I see only one issue: resistance grew up with 100

Hello,

I have successfully used xDrip, G5, Samsung Galaxy Note 5, Android 7.0 and Sony SmartWatch3 for a while, and planned to switch to the G6.

I inserted a new G6 Tx and sensor. I'm not using the Dexcom Rx.

I used the Source Wizard in xDrip, entering the Tx code, then later the senor code.

After a while I got a message about sensor failure and asking me if I wanted to do a hardware reset. I didn't. 

After 2 hrs I was asked to enter 2 blood calibrations, which I did.  I few minutes later it said "calibration rejected: sensor stopped".

I has appeared to get a few readings but no more. Its odd that there is a recent "Got Data" but also it says the sensor is "Stopped".

Any tips? Maybe there are some G5 settings left over? Would a re-install of xDrip help?

Thanks,
![Screenshot_20190415-141819](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/227969/56156195-b77c1a00-5f8a-11e9-863b-80eddceea966.png)
![Screenshot_20190415-141920](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/227969/56156212-c06ceb80-5f8a-11e9-9cad-ae0217c2ad68.png)

Never mind. It's working. I connected the Dexcom app for a while (after force killing xDrip) .  xDrip then restarted by itself after a while as I noticed it was getting done readings. I killed the Dexcom app. Working fine now.

I've ran a hard reset against 
```
G6 
Sensor Device: 8J****
Firmware V: 2.18.2.98
Other V: 0.48.69
Shelf Life: 65/365
Transmitter Days: 90
Sensor Status: OK 5.9 days
Bluetooth Link: Connected
Last Connected: 2 mintes
Preemptive restarts: Disabled
```
Although it did not work to reset the transmitter, it did not seem to "break" the transmitter. I continued to receive readings after the reset ran- but only after I rebooted the phone. Hopefully this information helps.

**Edit** This may be coincidence only, but I'm currently on day 97 on a firefly transmitter. The timeline was: couple hours of no readings, hard reset transmitter, reboot phone, readings again- day count not reset, now 97 days

**Edit Edit** Now currently on day 102, I am thinking maybe the hard reset did do something for the transmitter? Does anyone experience more than 90 days on the firefly?
@ulurujamman Unless you believe there is a bug in xDrip, associated with the experience you have described here, would you please close this issue?
